summary: From last complete quarter's gross revenue, the ladder splits it by café, follows each café's quarterly and monthly trend, separates visit frequency, customers and basket size for established versus new cafés, and ends by sizing three levers: basket, visit frequency and jaffle mix.

narration.text: Gross revenue in the last complete quarter, Q3 2026, was $649.1K, and that is the baseline next quarter has to beat.
Brooklyn brought in $318.1K of that, well ahead of Philadelphia at $195.4K, Chicago at $79.5K and San Francisco at $56.1K.

Month by month, Brooklyn fell from $115.8K in July to $93.0K in September and Philadelphia slipped from $71.0K to $57.3K, while Chicago rose from $12.8K to $32.0K and San Francisco from $1.0K to $25.9K.
Quarter on quarter, Brooklyn grew 57.2% in Q2 before slipping 6.1% in Q3, while Philadelphia was flat in Q2 at 0.2% and then fell 7.7%.
The monthly view shows the decline continuing into October, with Brooklyn down to $84.7K and Philadelphia to $55.3K.
The newer cafés moved the other way in October, with Chicago reaching $36.5K and San Francisco $32.0K.
To see what moves revenue, the Q3 drivers by store show that Brooklyn's 29,787 orders came from 699 customers, about 42.6 orders each at an average order of $10.68.

For the established cafés, customer numbers held near 1,147 through September, so the decline came from fewer visits per customer, which fell from 14.9 in July to 12.3 in September, while the average order stayed near $11.
The newer cafés are growing through reach, with Chicago customers rising from 208 in July to 257 in October and San Francisco from 111 to 228, at average orders of about $11.
Lift Brooklyn's average order from $10.68 to the chain average of $10.99, which the basket gap table sizes at about $9.3K for Q3, the largest of any store.
Win back visits at Brooklyn and Philadelphia first, since orders per customer fell from 15.6 to 12.8 at Brooklyn and from 14.0 to 11.4 at Philadelphia between July and September.
Push jaffles in every café, because they make up only 21.8% to 24.0% of units sold, with San Francisco lowest at 21.8% and Brooklyn at 22.5%.

digests.headline: $649.1K baseline
digests.summary: Gross revenue in Q3 2026, the last complete quarter, was $649.1K, which is the baseline next quarter has to beat.

digests.question: Which cafés drive the revenue?
digests.headline: Brooklyn $318.1K
digests.summary: Q3 2026 gross revenue was $649.1K, the baseline next quarter has to beat. Brooklyn contributed $318.1K and Philadelphia $195.4K, but both declined through the quarter while Chicago and San Francisco grew.

digests.question: How is each café trending?
digests.headline: Core cafés fading
digests.summary: Q3 2026 gross revenue was $649.1K, the baseline next quarter has to beat, led by Brooklyn at $318.1K and Philadelphia at $195.4K. Those two established cafés fell 6.1% and 7.7% in Q3 and kept falling in October, while Chicago and San Francisco kept growing.

digests.question: Why is revenue moving?
digests.headline: visits, not customers
digests.summary: Q3 2026 gross revenue was $649.1K, the baseline next quarter has to beat, led by Brooklyn at $318.1K and Philadelphia at $195.4K. Those two cafés fell because customers visited less often, not because customers left or spent less per order, while Chicago and San Francisco grew by adding customers.

digests.question: What should we do?
digests.headline: Basket, visits, jaffles
digests.summary: Q3 2026 gross revenue was $649.1K, led by Brooklyn at $318.1K and Philadelphia at $195.4K, and those two fell because customers visited less often, while Chicago and San Francisco grew by adding customers. Next quarter, win back visit frequency at the established cafés, lift Brooklyn's basket to the chain average, and raise the jaffle share of units.
